title: Iterative radix-2 divider + single shared 33x33 multiplier (kill 200ns combinational DIV path)
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz: the worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) is
clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> EX/MEM, i.e. the forwarding mux
feeding the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` operators in alu.sv
(four of them: signed/unsigned quotient and remainder, each an
array divider of ~32 ripple-subtract rows). Every other instruction pays
for this path on every cycle. CoreMark -O3 executes very few DIV/REM
instructions inside the timed region (list/matrix/state kernels are
add/mul/branch/load dominated), so making division slow in cycles but
removing it from the clock-period critical path is an overwhelmingly
favourable trade. The multiplier is also built three times
(mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su, each 64-bit) which wastes DSP/LUT area and adds
a wide 3-way result mux on the same EX path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. New module rtl/div_unit.sv: sequential restoring (radix-2,
   1 quotient bit/cycle) divider shared by DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU. On start it
   latches |a|, |b| (sign-magnitude for signed ops), result-sign flags,
   op kind, and the special cases (b==0 -> q=all-ones / r=a;
   INT_MIN/-1 -> q=INT_MIN / r=0, resolved up-front so they finish in 1
   cycle). 32 iterations of shift/compare/subtract on a 33-bit partial
   remainder, then one fix-up cycle that conditionally negates q or r.
   The per-cycle logic is one 33-bit subtract + mux, well under the
   remaining EX path. Operands MUST be latched at start (post-forward
   values), because instructions ahead drain from MEM/WB during the
   stall and the forwarding sources change.
2. EX-stage integration: when ID/EX holds a valid DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU and
   the divider has not yet produced its result, assert div_busy.
   hazard_unit: div_busy -> stall_if, stall_id (hold ID/EX, no flush),
   and the EX/MEM register captures a bubble (valid=0, reg_write=0,
   mem_read/mem_write=0) instead of holding, so older instructions keep
   draining through MEM/WB. On the done cycle the quotient/remainder is
   muxed into alu_result and the DIV advances normally. dmem_stall still
   has priority (freeze everything including the divider's start/done
   handshake). A small "done" flag in div_unit is cleared when the DIV
   leaves EX so back-to-back DIVs restart correctly. Redirect can never
   coincide with a DIV in EX (DIV is not a branch), but the flush path
   must still abort/reset the divider if ID/EX is flushed.
3. Remove `/` and `%` from alu.sv entirely (ALU_DIV..ALU_REMU arms
   return the div_unit result via ex_stage, not via alu). Under
   `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` keep the existing single-cycle
   (a-b)^const stand-ins and force div_busy=0, so the formal liveness
   check (depth 20) and all ALTOPS checks see exactly today's
   behaviour and timing; the real iterative path is only built when
   ALTOPS is undefined (sim/cosim/FPGA).
4. Replace the three 64-bit multipliers with ONE signed 33x33 product:
   a_ext = {a[31] & a_signed, a}, b_ext = {b[31] & b_signed, b}, where
   a_signed = MULH|MULHSU, b_signed = MULH. out = op==MUL ? p[31:0] :
   p[63:32]. This maps to a single Gowin MULT36X36 (or 4x MULT18X18)
   instead of three, trims the LUT result mux, and shortens the new
   critical path (fwd mux -> multiplier -> EX/MEM).
Expected: the critical path collapses from ~200 ns to the
forward-mux -> 33x33 DSP multiply (or 32-bit adder/branch compare ->
redirect -> PC) path, plausibly 30-45 ns, i.e. Fmax 5.4 -> 22-33 MHz
(4-6x). CPI cost: ~34 extra cycles per DIV/REM; CoreMark's timed loop
has only a handful of divisions per iteration versus ~300k cycles per
iteration, so iter/cycle drops by well under 1%. Net fitness gain is
several hundred percent (schema caps the estimate at +50).

title: Move RV32M out of the 1-cycle EX ALU into a multi-cycle MulDiv unit (iterative divider + operand-registered DSP multiplier)
motivation:
The baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz. The worst path is 199.8 ns deep with 150 logic
levels: MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> EX operand mux -> alu.sv -> EX/MEM
(dmem address register). alu.sv builds DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU with combinational
SystemVerilog `/` and `%`, which is a 32-stage array divider (several
subtract-and-select rows per quotient bit). It also builds three separate
64-bit products (mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su), which use 6 DSPs, and puts them
behind the forwarding muxes. The divider alone accounts for most of the
12.3k LUT4s and almost all of the critical path. CoreMark's timed region
runs almost no divides and relatively few multiplies. So every ALU
instruction pays a ~190 ns cycle-time cost for an operation that is almost
never executed. IPC is fine: about 2.2 CoreMark/MHz, which already meets
the core.yaml target. Frequency is what is broken. Changing the structure
of the M-extension datapath is the single highest-leverage change available.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take the M-extension out of the single-cycle ALU and put it in a dedicated
multi-cycle `muldiv` unit next to the ALU in EX. The pipeline stalls while
the unit is busy (a structural hazard handled like dmem stall).

1. New rtl/muldiv.sv. It is a small FSM (IDLE -> BUSY -> DONE) with these
   parts:
   - start: fires when ID/EX holds a valid `is_muldiv` instruction and the
     unit has no finished-but-unconsumed result for it. On start it
     registers the post-forward rs1/rs2 values and the op. This puts a flop
     between the forwarding muxes and all M-ext arithmetic, which removes
     the fwd->ALU->mul/div path.
   - multiply: a single 33x33 signed multiplier on the captured operands.
     Sign extension is a_ext = {a[31] & a_is_signed, a}, and the same form
     for b. This covers MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU with one DSP array
     instead of three. The 64-bit product is registered into the result
     register one cycle after capture, so a MUL costs 1 stall cycle. If
     `make timing` still shows the DSP path as critical, add one more
     pipeline register (2 stall cycles).
   - divide: a radix-2 restoring divider over |a| and |b|, one quotient bit
     per cycle for 32 cycles, then a sign fix-up for quotient and
     remainder. Two cases finish in one cycle at start: divide-by-zero
     (q = all ones, r = dividend) and INT_MIN / -1 (q = INT_MIN, r = 0).
     These match the RV32M semantics that alu.sv encodes today.
   - done/hold: once `done` is set, the result stays in the register and
     `done` stays high until EX actually advances (!stall_ex_mem). This
     keeps the result correct when a dmem stall freezes EX/MEM on the same
     cycle. It also prevents the same instruction from being restarted.
   - `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`: the same FSM and handshake, but the result is
     the existing ALTOPS formula computed from the captured operands, and
     every op completes after one busy cycle. Formal therefore still
     proves the new stall, hold and forwarding behaviour within the
     depth-20 insn and liveness budget. A 34-cycle divide would otherwise
     overflow that budget.
2. alu.sv drops every M-ext arm (the mul_* products, `/` and `%`). It
   becomes a pure RV32I ALU: add/sub, logic ops, compares, shifts and LUI.
3. ex_stage.sv:
   - Instantiates muldiv.
   - Raises `md_stall` while an M op is in EX and the unit is not done.
     During md_stall, EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, reg_write=0,
     mem_read/write=0) unless a dmem stall is holding it.
   - On completion, alu_result is the muldiv result register.
   - The M op's RVFI rs1_val/rs2_val/write_data come from the muldiv
     captured operands, not from the live forward muxes. After a
     multi-cycle stall the forwarding sources have drained into bubbles,
     and the ID/EX regfile snapshot may be stale, so the live muxes can
     give the wrong value.
4. hazard_unit.sv gets an `md_stall` input:
   - It asserts stall_if and stall_id.
   - It suppresses flush_id. A load-use bubble must not delete the M op
     that is held in ID/EX. This uses the same precedence rule that
     dmem_stall already has.
   - It drives a new `bubble_ex_mem` output.
   - dmem_stall keeps priority over md_stall for the EX/MEM hold.
5. decoder.sv/core_pkg.sv: add ctrl_t.is_muldiv. It is set only inside the
   already-validated funct7=0000001 OP arm, so the illegal-default
   discipline is unchanged.

Expected result:
- The critical path collapses to a normal 5-stage RV32I path: forward mux
  -> 32-bit add/compare/shift -> EX/MEM or branch redirect -> PC/imem.
  That should be on the order of 15-25 levels on GW2A, a plausible 40-70
  MHz. This is roughly 8-12x the current 5.44 MHz.
- LUT4 count should fall by several thousand cells, likely under the 10k
  target, and DSP use drops from 6 to about 4.
- IPC cost is 1 extra cycle per MUL (a few percent of dynamic CoreMark
  instructions are multiplies in matrix_*) and about 34 cycles per DIV/REM
  (almost none in the timed region). That is an estimated 3-6% IPC loss,
  against a >8x Fmax gain. The estimated fitness is well beyond +50%, the
  schema's maximum.

title: Decode-in-fetch branch predictor: JAL/branch redirect in IF with BTFN-biased 2-bit BHT + tiny RAS
motivation:
The bench core resolves every control transfer in EX and always predicts
fall-through. Because IF and ID share one cycle (imem is zero-latency and
there is no IF/ID flop), each taken branch, JAL and JALR costs exactly one
squashed fetch cycle. Measured with the reference ISS on the canonical
CoreMark ELF (2K, -O3, timed region only, 2.92M instructions = 292k/iter):
conditional branches 18.1% of instructions (55.6% taken), JAL 1.7%,
JALR 0.47% (all of them plain `ret`). That is 0.1224 redirect bubbles per
instruction. Baseline 12.12 iter/s at 5.442 MHz = 449k cycles/iter, so
CPI is ~1.54, and ~8% of all cycles are fall-through-prediction
bubbles. Trace-driven model of the proposed predictor: 64-entry
BTFN-agree table + JAL-in-IF + 2-entry RAS leaves 0.0159 bubbles/insn
(branch mispredicts 46.3k, RAS misses 101). Alternatives measured: static
BTFN+JAL without RAS 0.0427, bimodal-64 0.0178, agree-256 0.0136. So
64-entry agree is the sweet spot. The current Fmax limiter is the
combinational divider in EX (~200 ns path), so small IF-side logic is
timing-free today, and stays sub-critical (~10-15 ns) even after a sibling
hypothesis fixes the divider.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Because the fetched instruction word is available combinationally in the
same cycle as its PC, the core can compute the *exact* direct target in IF
without a BTB: pre-decode imem_data for JAL (opcode 1101111), BRANCH
(1100011) and JALR (1100111), extract the J/B immediate and form
pc + imm with a dedicated adder. Next-PC priority becomes:
  EX redirect (mispredict repair) > stall hold > IF prediction > pc+4.
Predictions are only made when the IF slot is genuinely valid
(imem_ready && !stall_if && !redirect), and only when the predicted target
is word-aligned (imm[1]==0) so misaligned-target traps keep their current
"no redirect, pc_next=pc+4" semantics untouched.
  * JAL: always redirect in IF (100% accurate; EX never redirects a
    predicted JAL).
  * Conditional branches: direction from a 64-entry 2-bit counter table
    indexed by pc[7:2], operated as an "agree" predictor against static
    BTFN (counter MSB=1 means "agree with BTFN": backward=taken,
    forward=not-taken). Reset all counters to weakly-agree, so cold
    branches behave as BTFN and the table learns data-dependent forward
    branches (core_list_find / core_state_transition compares).
    Updated from EX with the resolved outcome, once per branch
    (gated by !stall_ex_mem so dmem-stall-held branches don't
    over-train).
  * Returns: 2-entry return-address stack. Push pc+4 in IF for JAL/JALR
    with rd in {x1,x5}; pop and predict on JALR with rs1 in {x1,x5},
    rd==x0 (plain `ret`). Pushes/pops are gated by the same IF-valid
    condition, so the single wrong-path IF slot squashed by an EX
    redirect never corrupts the stack.
A `pred_taken` bit (and for JALR the 32-bit `pred_target`) is carried in
if_id_t -> id_ex_t. EX repair: for branches, redirect iff
branch_taken != pred_taken, to branch_target or pc+4 respectively; for
JAL, redirect only if not predicted (e.g. misaligned case already traps
without redirect); for JALR, redirect iff !pred_taken ||
pred_target != {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0}. pc_next/RVFI stay the architectural
values computed in EX, so RVFI, formal pc_fwd/pc_bwd and cosim are
unaffected; the hazard unit keeps flushing only the one IF slot on an EX
redirect. Consistency argument: ID/EX captures an IF instruction in
exactly the cycles the PC advances past it without an EX redirect
(!dmem_stall && !load_use && !redirect; imem_stall captures a
valid=0 NOP with pred_taken=0). So the latched pred bit always matches
the fetch decision actually taken, and the only wrong-path slot (IF,
squashed by the EX redirect) never touches the BHT/RAS. Expected: 87% of
redirect bubbles removed, 0.106 CPI saved (1.54 -> 1.43, +7.4%
iter/cycle). Fmax should be unchanged because the added IF path
(imem/LFSR reg -> predecode -> 32b add -> PC mux) is ~10-15 ns against
the ~200 ns EX divider path. The RAS is worth only ~0.3%, so drop it
first if it causes trouble. The BHT (~2%) and JAL/backward-branch

motivation:
The champion (hyp-20260929-002-r1s1, 48.67 MHz, 103.98 iter/s) has one
dominant critical path, identical in all three seeds: 21 logic levels /
48 cells, modules u_id -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id, ending at
the ID/EX register (id_ex_w.rs2_val_*). Walking the RTL:
  ID/EX -> forward mux -> branch comparators -> branch_cond -> redirect
  (u_ex) -> if_stage `out.instr = (flush||redirect) ? NOP : imem_data`
  (u_if) -> hazard_unit load-use 5-bit rd==rs1/rs2 compares ->
  stall_id / flush_id (u_hazard) -> sync-clear/CE of the ~200-bit
  ID/EX register (u_id).
The redirect also fans out through the NOP mux into the regfile read
addresses, decoder and imm_gen that feed ID/EX's D inputs. That entire
u_if -> u_hazard segment is logically redundant: whenever redirect=1
the ID/EX register is either flushed (flush_id already ORs redirect) or
held (dmem_stall/md_stall), so the wrong-path instruction's decode and
its load-use result are don't-cares. The redirect is only *needed* at
the PC mux and at flush_id. LESSONS for r1s1/r1s2 already call out this

divider left EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make EX's redirect reach the pipeline control through one LUT, and make
that control net small:

1. if_stage: drop `redirect` from the IF->ID bundle. out.instr =
   imem_stall ? NOP : imem_data and out.valid = !imem_stall (flush input
   = imem_stall only; io_imemReady comes from a registered stall
   generator so this mux is early). Wrong-path instructions after a
   taken branch/jump are now killed exclusively by flush_id. The PC
   register keeps its redirect-overrides-stall priority unchanged.
2. hazard_unit: flush_if = imem_stall (no redirect). load_use is now
   computed from early signals only (ID/EX regs + stall-gated imem
   word), so stall_id = dmem_stall | load_use | md_stall is entirely
   off the redirect path, and flush_id = (load_use | redirect) &
   !dmem_stall & !md_stall is a single LUT after redirect. Equivalence:
   when redirect=1 either flush_id=1 (flush beats stall in ID/EX) or
   dmem_stall/md_stall=1 (ID/EX holds), so load_use is a don't-care;
   when imem_stall=1 a spurious load-use only turns a valid=0 NOP bubble
   into a '0 bubble. core.sv wiring stays the same.

title: Squash-at-latch front end: cut the EX-redirect -> IF/ID payload -> decode/regfile/hazard -> ID/EX loop
motivation:
Champion (r1s1) runs at 48.67 MHz with a 25.7 ns / 21-level critical path
whose module trace is  ID/EX -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id  (ending
at ID/EX.rs2_val). That is two pipeline stages' worth of logic executed in
series in one cycle:
  1. EX: forward mux -> 32-bit branch compare -> redirect,
  2. IF: redirect forces the combinational IF/ID payload to NOP
     (out.instr = (flush||redirect) ? 0x13 : imem_data), so the
     instruction word itself now depends on redirect,
  3. ID: that muxed word feeds the decoder, the regfile read addresses
     (rs1/rs2 = instr[19:15]/[24:20]), the write-first bypass compare and
     the hazard unit's load-use compare,
  4. hazard: load_use -> stall_id / flush_id -> the sync-reset + enable of
     the whole ~250-bit ID/EX register (high-fanout SR/CE nets).
Measured on the champion with `make timing TARGET=bench` (place_option 0,
48.93 MHz), path 1 cell by cell: clock->Q of the regfile BSRAM (Gowin maps
the regfile to 2 BSRAMs and retimes ID/EX.rs?_val into the BSRAM address
register) 7.59 ns -> write-first bypass 2 LUTs -> EX forward mux 2 LUTs ->
29-cell carry-chain branch comparator done at 13.80 ns -> u_if/n330
(redirect||flush, 5 LUTs, fanout 104 = the NOP mux) 18.04 ns ->
rs1_addr_w (NOP-muxed rs address, fanout 6) 19.12 ns -> hazard load-use
carry-chain compare 20.75 ns -> u_id stall/flush 22.27 ns -> ID/EX
rs2_val hold/flush mux select (fanout 33) 24.39 ns -> D at 25.73 ns.
About 12 ns of the 20.4 ns data path comes after the EX comparator
and exists only because redirect is fed back into the fetched word.
The NOP substitution is redundant: every case in which it matters is
already covered by flush_id (redirect => ID/EX captures a bubble anyway)
or by an ID/EX hold (dmem_stall / md_stall). The imem word itself comes
straight from a flop (LFSR in the timed wrapper, zero-latency imem in
cosim), so without the NOP mux the whole decode/regfile/hazard cone starts
at a register instead of at the end of EX. LESSONS.md (r1s1) already
identified this regfile -> hazard/stall -> ID/EX capture path as the
limiter now that the divider is gone.

latch", so the EX redirect never feeds the front-end datapath:

1. if_stage: out.instr = imem_data unconditionally (no redirect/flush
   NOP mux); out.valid = imem_ready (a flop in the bench). The redirect

   rs1/rs2 vs ID/EX.rd (registered). A spurious load-use from a
   wrong-path or not-ready word is harmless: redirect already overrides
   stall_if at the PC, flush_id already bubbles ID/EX on redirect, and on
   imem stall the PC holds and ID/EX takes a bubble either way. The
   if_rs inputs no longer depend on redirect, so stall_if/stall_id are
   functions of flops only (imem_ready, dmem_ready, EX/MEM ctrl, ID/EX
   rd/mem_read, md_done state, raw instr). flush_if is deleted.
3. id_stage ID/EX register split in two:

   bubble with stale payload is architecturally inert — the same
   property the EX/MEM `bubble` and MEM/WB `hold_wb` paths already rely
   on.

   stall/hold semantics and RVFI generation exactly as today (RVFI only

title: IF-stage JAL/BHT fetch predictor with registered (next-cycle) mispredict redirect to take branch resolve off the critical path
motivation:
The champion (hyp-002-r1s1, 103.98 iter/s, 48.67 MHz, 4.68M cycles for 10
iterations, CPI about 1.60) is now limited by the branch-redirect path.
The reported worst path (25.7 ns, 21 levels) runs
u_rf/regs (the ID/EX rs value that Gowin packed into the regfile RAM output)
-> u_ex (forward mux -> 32-bit compare -> branch_cond -> redirect)
-> u_if (instr NOP mux on redirect) -> u_hazard (load-use rs compare ->
stall_id/flush_id) -> u_id (ID/EX register CE/SR, fanout over ~150 flops).
The EX redirect also drives the IF NOP mux into the decoder -> ID/EX.ctrl
and the PC mux, so it is combinational into every front-end register.
Control flow is also the largest CPI loss that remains. The r1s2 trace
study on the canonical CoreMark ELF found 18.1% conditional branches (55.6%
taken), 1.7% JAL and 0.47% JALR, for 0.122 redirect bubbles per
instruction. That is about 357k of the 4.68M timed cycles (7.6%). r1s2
measured a +6.9% cycle reduction from an IF predictor on the baseline, but
it kept the combinational EX redirect, and the lesson warns that adding
prediction gating to that path costs Fmax once the divider is gone.
A good predictor makes mispredicts rare. That makes it cheap to delay the
redirect by one cycle and cut the path that currently limits Fmax.

prediction gating to that path costs Fmax once the divider is gone.

redirect by one cycle and cut the path that currently limits Fmax.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a zero-bubble fetch predictor in IF. With accurate prediction in place,
move mispredict repair from a combinational EX signal to a registered
signal that acts one cycle later. The mispredict penalty goes from 1 to 2
cycles, but only about 0.02 mispredicts/insn remain. No EX-computed signal
then reaches the PC, the IF/ID payload, the hazard unit or the ID/EX
enable in the same cycle.

1. IF predictor. imem_data is an LFSR flop on the FPGA bench and
   zero-latency in sim, so this path is short.
   - Pre-decode io_imemData for JAL (1101111) and BRANCH (1100011).
     Extract the J/B immediate and form pred_target = pc + imm with a
     dedicated adder. The exact target is known in IF, so no BTB is
     needed.
   - Branch direction comes from a 64-entry x 2-bit table indexed by
     pc[7:2]. It runs as an "agree with BTFN" predictor, as in r1s2: the
     counter MSB means "agree with static backward-taken /
     forward-not-taken". Counters reset to weakly-agree. This was the best
     size/accuracy point in the r1s2 trace model: 0.0159 mispredicts/insn.
   - pred_taken = (is_jal || (is_branch && dir)) && pred_target[1:0]==0
     && !imem_stall. A misaligned target is never predicted, so the
     existing trap-with-no-redirect / pc_next=pc+4 semantics are
     unchanged.
   - Next-PC priority: redirect_q ? ex_mem.pc_next : stall_if ? pc :
     pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4. The prediction needs no gating from
     stall or redirect, because the stall/redirect arms override it in the
     mux.

     exactly when the PC advances using that decision, so the latched bit
     always matches the path actually fetched. When imem stalls, the slot
     is a valid=0 NOP with pred_taken=0.

     about 0.6% CPI, which is not worth a 32-bit compare in EX or
     speculative-stack repair.

   - branch: mispredict = branch_taken != pred_taken
   - JAL: mispredict = !pred_taken
   - JALR: always mispredict

   "EX/MEM captures this instruction this cycle" (!stall_ex_mem;
   md_stall is never set for a branch).
   Add a 1-bit flop: redirect_q <= mispredict. The target does not need a
   new register: EX/MEM.pc_next already holds the architectural next PC
   (target, or pc+4 for a predicted-taken branch that was not taken, or
   pc+4 on a misalign trap). The IF redirect uses ex_mem.pc_next while
   redirect_q is set. pc_next and RVFI remain architectural, so formal
   pc_fwd/pc_bwd and cosim are unaffected.
   - The BHT update comes from EX under the same valid && !kill &&
     advance gating, once per branch. Its write port is a flop/LUTRAM
     write and is off the critical path.

   flop). While redirect_q is high, the mispredicted control instruction
   is in EX/MEM (not a memory op, so dmem_stall is 0 that cycle). ID/EX
   holds wrong-path i+1 and IF holds wrong-path i+2.
   - flush_id |= redirect_q, unconditionally. The ID/EX content is always
     wrong-path, and IF slot i+2 must not be captured.
   - bubble_ex_mem |= redirect_q, so i+1 does not enter EX/MEM.

     FSM. Otherwise it would reach DONE and hand a stale result to the
     next M op. md_stall is then 0 in that cycle.
   - Gate i+1's own mispredict/redirect and BHT update with !kill.
   - flush_if = redirect_q || imem_stall. The IF NOP mux and the hazard
     unit's rs compare now depend only on flops (redirect_q, imem_ready,
     LFSR imem_data).

   `redirect` becomes redirect_q with the unconditional flush above.
   Load-use detection still reads the (now flop-driven) IF instruction.

title: Flatten the EX operand path: LUT-RAM regfile + ID-precomputed one-hot forward selects + dedicated AGU for dmem address
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (r2s0, 132.16 iter/s, 60.7-61.9
MHz, CPI fixed at 4.68M cycles) shows the top 25 setup paths all start at
the register file, which Gowin mapped to BSRAM (BSRAM 6 = 4 dmem + 2
regfile copies). They fan out to pc_hi CE/D, the ID/EX live-bit RESET
(flush_id), EX/MEM.alu_result D, and the dmem BSRAM ADB (EX/MEM.alu_result
absorbed as the dmem address register). All of them are within 0.15 ns of
the 16.44 ns worst path. Cell by cell, the worst path is:
  BSRAM regs CLK->DO tC2Q ............... 2.26 ns
  u_id rs2_val_30_s15 (write-first bypass/x0 mux, retimed AFTER the
       BSRAM output register) ........... 0.78
  u_ex rs2_30_s10 / s8 / s7 (3 LUT levels of forward mux: fwd_sel
       priority + 3:1 mux + WB mem_to_reg mux) + routing ... 4.40
  branch compare carry (n306/n307) ...... 2.4 (incl. 1.8 route)
  6 LUTs of branch_cond->redirect->PC CE . ~5.9
So ~7.4 ns of every critical path goes to getting the operand out of
the register file and through forwarding, before any arithmetic starts.
Every address compare and select involved is known a cycle earlier, in
ID. The dmem-ADB paths also go through the whole ALU result mux
(op case mux + is_jump/is_muldiv mux) because the address is
EX/MEM.alu_result.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three micro-opts on the shared operand path. There is no CPI change; this is all Fmax.

1. Regfile in distributed LUT-RAM, not BSRAM. Put
   (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) on `regs`. Reads become
   asynchronous RAM16SDP reads from the IF word (the bench's imem word
   is a flop), finished on the ID side (x0 mux + write-first bypass stay
   here, BEFORE the flop). The ID/EX payload rs1_val/rs2_val become
   plain DFFs: tC2Q ~0.4 ns instead of BSRAM's 2.26 ns, and the bypass
   LUT leaves the EX path. The ID-side path (imem flop -> RAM16 read ->
   depth MUX2 -> bypass -> DFF) is ~5 levels, far from critical. Keep
   the reset loop only if Gowin still infers LUT-RAM with it. Check
   `make timing`: BSRAM drops 6->4, LUT-RAM rises, FF stays ~700.
   If the reset loop blocks inference, drop it (x0 is still forced to
   0 by the read mux; cosim/formal never read unwritten regs before
   crt0 sets them). Do this only after confirming cosim passes.

2. Registered one-hot forward selects computed in ID. For each rs, ID
   computes from the IF/ID rs field and the CURRENT pipeline regs
   (= what EX/MEM and MEM/WB will hold when this instruction is in EX;
   whenever ID/EX captures (!stall_id) EX/MEM and MEM/WB both advance):
     s_exm = ID/EX live_reg_write && !jump_misalign_trap && rd!=0 && rd==rs
             (jump_misalign_trap = is_jump && (is_jalr ? jalr_sum[1] : imm[1]),
              exported from EX; jalr_sum[1] needs only the 2 LSBs)
     s_mwb = !s_exm && EX/MEM reg_write && !mem_misalign && rd!=0 && rd==rs
     s_rf  = !s_exm && !s_mwb
   These load into the ID/EX payload with CE = !stall. EX's operand is then
     (s_rf & rs_val_q) | (s_exm & EX/MEM.alu_result) | (s_mwb & MEM/WB.wb_data)
   which is 2 LUT levels, with no compare and no priority chain. MEM/WB
   gets a pre-muxed wb_data field (mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result,
   muxed before the flop, off-critical), which also feeds the regfile
   write, so wb_stage is just wires. forward_unit is deleted.
   Held-select correctness: on dmem_stall, EX/MEM holds and MEM/WB
   keeps its data (hold_mem_wb clears valid only), so the held selects
   stay exact. This is the same contract the old forward_unit relied on
   (it keyed on reg_write, not valid). On md_stall, muldiv captured the
   post-forward operands on the first EX cycle (a_cap/b_cap feed the
   result and RVFI), so later selects are don't-cares. Flushed ID/EX
   entries have their live bits cleared, so their selects are inert.

3. Dedicated AGU for the dmem address. EX computes agu = rs1 + imm with
   its own adder and registers it as EX/MEM.mem_addr. mem_stage drives
   dmem_addr, the byte mask, the misalign check and RVFI mem_addr from
   it. The Gowin-absorbed dmem address register then sits behind
   operand mux -> adder only, not behind the ALU op case mux and the
   is_jump/is_muldiv result mux. alu_result is unchanged for
   forwarding/WB.

Estimate: this removes about 1.8 ns (tC2Q) + 0.8 ns (bypass) + about
1.3 ns (one forward-mux level plus routing) from every top path, and
about 1-2 ns more from the dmem-ADB family. 16.4 ns -> about 12.5 ns
gives about 61 -> 78 MHz at identical CPI. The redirect tail (6 LUTs
after the compare) is then the likely next limiter. If `make timing`
shows it on top, flatten it by registering from ID one-hot branch
enables (lt/!lt/eq/!eq, pre-gated by !imm[1]) as flush-cleared live
bits, so redirect = OR of (enable & compare bit). That is optional.

title: Resolve operand forwarding in ID (registered, fully-bypassed EX operands) so the regfile read and fwd mux leave the EX cycle
motivation:
The champion's (r2s0, 61.86 MHz) worst path starts at the register-file RAM
cell (cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s0) and ends at cpu/u_if/pc_hi, and the next
path (seen in r2s1/r2s2 at ~22.4-23.1 ns) runs regs -> u_id -> u_ex -> alu ->
dmem BSRAM. A path from the RAM to pc_hi in one cycle is only possible
because synthesis pushed the ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val flops back onto the RAM
read address (registered-address read). So the "EX" cycle actually contains:
RAM read -> x0/write-first bypass mux -> 3:1 forward mux (EX/MEM, MEM/WB) ->
33-bit compare / 32-bit adder -> redirect -> PC mux (or -> dmem BSRAM address
register, which also absorbed the EX/MEM.alu_result flop). The earlier
redirect de-fanning (r2s0) and registered-redirect/predictor (r2s2) attempts
both left that operand front end alone, which is why they stall at ~60 MHz.
Removing three to four LUT levels plus the RAM read from the EX cycle should
raise Fmax a lot without costing any CPI.

Confirmed with `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (place_option 0,
60.7 MHz). The regfile is mapped to BSRAM (regs_regs_0_0_s0 @ BSRAM_R28).
Worst path, data portion 16.44 ns:
  BSRAM CLKB->DO tC2Q 2.26 ns
  -> u_id/id_ex_w.rs2_val_30_s15 (x0/write-first bypass LUT that synthesis
     left after the absorbed ID/EX flop)
  -> u_ex/rs2_30_s10 -> s8 -> s7 (3-LUT forward mux, ~1.6+1.0+0.7 ns route)
  -> u_ex/n306/n307 compare carry -> u_if/n69 / u_ex/n1153 redirect logic
  -> pc_hi CE (fanout 30).
7.4 ns of the 16.44 ns is spent before the comparator starts. A plain FF
(tC2Q ~0.4 ns) feeding the comparator directly removes ~6-7 ns from this
path, which leaves other EX paths as the limit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the operand datapath so that EX only sees flops. Forwarding moves
from the start of EX to the end of ID. The ID/EX register captures the final
post-bypass operand value, and the ALU, branch comparator, AGU, muldiv and
store data read ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val directly. EX has no forward mux.

ID-stage operand select, per source (rs1, rs2), in priority order:
  1. EX producer: ID/EX.rd == rs && EX live reg_write (after misalign-trap
     adjustment, i.e. ctrl_with_trap.reg_write, which is cheap: imm[1] or
     jalr_sum[1]) && rd != 0 -> ex_result, where ex_result is the same value
     EX/MEM.alu_result is about to capture (is_jump ? pc+4 : is_muldiv ?
     md_result : alu_result). Export it from ex_stage as a new output.
  2. MEM producer: EX/MEM.rd == rs && MEM-stage trap-adjusted reg_write
     (EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write && !mem_misalign) && rd != 0 ->
     mem_result = mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result. Export load_data /
     mem_result from mem_stage.
  3. Register file read (the existing write-first bypass already covers the
     WB producer, so no separate MEM/WB forward is needed).

their live bits), so only the data inputs are late. The late data inputs are
ALU -> result mux -> fwd mux -> ID/EX, one mux level after the ALU. Today the
equivalent path is one mux level before the ALU, so it is no deeper. Because
the RAM output now feeds a mux whose other inputs are unregistered, synthesis
can no longer retime ID/EX into the RAM address, and the RAM read stays in
the ID cycle: LFSR/imem flop -> LUT-RAM -> bypass -> fwd -> ID/EX.

!(dmem_stall || load_use || md_stall). EX/MEM also advances in exactly those

producer in EX with its final result. A load in EX is still covered by the
existing 1-cycle load-use bubble. On the next cycle the load is in MEM, and

happens while the bus stalls. An M op in EX holds ID via md_stall, and on the
done cycle md_result is forwarded. Load-use, branch and M-op penalties stay
the same, so CoreMark cycles stay at 4,680,666.

stalled, because every producer of that instruction was older and was
already resolved when it was captured.

title: Lean IF branch predictor on r2s0: 1-cycle mismatch redirect at unchanged EX logic depth
motivation:
Champion r2s0 runs 132.16 iter/s: 61.86 MHz and 4,680,666 timed cycles for
10 iterations (CPI about 1.6). Every taken branch, JAL and JALR still costs
one bubble, because EX redirects and kills the instruction in IF. The r1s2
trace study measured 18.1% conditional branches (55.6% taken), 1.7% JAL and
0.47% JALR. That is about 0.122 redirect bubbles per instruction, or ~7.6% of
cycles, the largest CPI loss the front end still controls.
Two earlier predictor attempts show where the value is and why it did not
land:
 - r2s2 (IF predecode + 64x2 agree-BTFN BHT, registered 2-cycle redirect)
   cut cycles by 5.1% (4.68M -> 4.44M), even with the doubled mispredict
   penalty. But it added +472 LUT4 / +172 FF, and median Fmax fell 5.1%
   (58.7 MHz). The worst path was the unrelated EX fwd -> ALU -> dmem-BSRAM
   path, which suggests the area/congestion slowed placement. The predictor
   arm itself was not the problem. Registering the redirect bought no Fmax
   because the ALU -> dmem path (~22.4 ns) is co-critical with r2s0's
   redirect -> PC path (21.8 ns).
 - Lesson (LESSONS.md, r2s2): re-stack the predictor's CPI gain on r2s0
   only if the prediction arm stays off the ~62 MHz critical path.
So the target is the r2s2 cycle saving plus the ~1 extra cycle per
mispredict it gave back, with an adder-light, flop-light predictor. The EX
redirect must keep exactly r2s0's LUT depth. The IF prediction arm must be
fed only by flops (PC register, imem word: on the FPGA bench io_imemData is
an LFSR flop), and it must enter the PC mux below the late redirect arm.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a zero-bubble fetch predictor in IF. Keep r2s0's combinational EX redirect,
but have it fire only on a mispredict, so the mispredict penalty stays 1 cycle.
All prediction-dependent terms EX needs are folded into ID/EX flops, so
EX's redirect equation keeps the same gate structure as today.

1. IF predecode and target (if_stage.sv)
   - Decode io_imemData for JAL (opcode 1101111) and BRANCH (1100011, funct3
     not 2/3). Extract the J/B immediate and compute
     pred_target[31:2] = pc_hi + imm[31:2] with one 30-bit adder. Both inputs
     are flops.
   - Direction: a 64-entry x 2-bit "agree with BTFN" counter table indexed by
     pc[7:2], read asynchronously from the PC register. Use LUTRAM-friendly
     inference: async read, one sync write port, and no reset loop over the
     array. If the tool needs an init, use an initial block set to
     weakly-agree. r1s2's trace model found this size/scheme best: 0.0159
     mispredicts/insn. counter MSB=1 means "agree with static
     backward-taken / forward-not-taken", and the static direction is
     imm sign = instr[31].
   - pred_taken = !flush && (is_jal || (is_branch && dir)) && !imm[1]. A
     misaligned target is never predicted, so the existing EX
     trap-without-redirect semantics stay valid.
   - PC mux priority: redirect ? redirect_target : stall ? hold :
     pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4. The EX redirect stays the last and
     latest mux level, as in r2s0. pred_taken needs no stall/redirect gating
     because the higher-priority arms override it.
   - Export in if_id_t: pred_taken plus alt_pc[31:2], the PC to repair to if
     EX disagrees: pred_taken ? pc+4 : pred_target. That is a 30-bit 2:1
     mux of values IF already computes.
2. ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv)
   - Put pred_taken / alt_pc in the early-CE payload register (not the
     flush-cleared live bits), plus two pre-folded bits:
       br_inv_q    = funct3[0] ^ pred_taken
       jal_redir_q = is_jump && !is_jalr && !pred_taken && !imm[1]
     They are only consumed under live_branch_q / live_jump_q, which the
     existing flush clears, so the flush fanout does not grow.
   - ID/EX captures an IF slot exactly when the PC advances using that same
     prediction. Stalls hold both the PC and ID/EX. An imem-stall slot is a
     valid=0 NOP with pred_taken=0. A redirect flushes ID/EX. So the latched
     bit always describes the path that was actually fetched, even if the
     BHT was updated while the slot was stalled.
3. EX (ex_stage.sv): mismatch redirect with no added LUT levels
   - Today: branch_cond = op[2] ? (lt ^ op[0]) : (eq ^ op[0]). New:
     mismatch_br = op[2] ? (lt ^ br_inv_q) : (eq ^ br_inv_q). Same
     structure; op[0] is replaced by another registered bit.
   - redirect = (is_branch && mismatch_br && !imm[1]) || jal_redir_q ||
     (is_jalr && !jalr_sum[1]). A predicted-taken branch or JAL that is
     correct never redirects. The misaligned-branch case keeps pred=0, so
     mismatch == taken and the imm[1] gate suppresses it, as the
     misalign_fault term does today. The JALR misalign gate is unchanged.
   - redirect_target = is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:2],00} : {alt_pc_q,00}. This
     removes EX's pc+imm adders from the redirect-target path, so the
     target path gets shorter.
   - Architectural branch_taken, pc_next, ctrl_with_trap and the RVFI fields
     are computed exactly as today. The pc+imm adders remain only for
     RVFI pc_next, which synthesis prunes.
   - BHT update port: when a valid branch leaves EX (live_branch_q &&
     !stall && !bubble), write counter[pc[7:2]] toward (taken == BTFN
     static direction). One write per branch; the update is a sync write
     with no timing impact.
4. Hazard unit: unchanged. flush_id still ORs the (now mismatch-only)
   redirect. No new kill machinery is needed, because the penalty stays at
   one killed slot, exactly as r2s0.
5. No RAS and no JALR prediction. JALR is 0.47% of instructions at 1 bubble,
   under 0.3% of cycles, and not worth a 30-bit compare on the forwarded-rs1
   path.

Expected effect
- Cycles: taken-control bubbles drop from ~0.122/insn to ~0.016 (BHT
  mispredicts) + 0.005 (JALR). r2s2 measured -238k cycles with a
  2-cycle mispredict penalty. Keeping the penalty at 1 cycle returns roughly
  another 25-35k, so expect about 4.68M -> 4.41-4.43M (-5.5 to -6%).
- Fmax: redirect enable and target have the same or lower depth, the
  prediction arm is flop-fed and below the redirect mux arm, and the area
  added is about 90-120 LUT4 + ~35 FF (1 adder, 64x2 LUTRAM, 30-bit alt_pc
  mux/flops), roughly a quarter of r2s2's. The target is 61-62 MHz, within
  P&R noise of r2s0.
- Fitness: about 132.16 * 1.06, roughly 140 (+6%), just above the 4.6% bar.
  If `make timing` shows the pred_target adder or BHT read on the worst
  path, fall back to predicting only backward branches + JAL (BTFN, no
  table). That keeps ~70% of the gain with even less logic.

title: Level-trim both EX limiters: 1-LUT operand forward (MEM-stage fwd moved to ID + imm/pc folding), one-hot ALU result select, CE-free PC
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on r3s0 (placement option 0: 97.9 MHz, 10.18 ns data
delay; the median across options is 88.9 MHz). The top 25 paths split into two families
that are tied within 0.02 ns, so fixing only one of them gains nothing:
 A) ALU, 15.508 ns, 11 cells: pay_q.fwd_rs1_exm -> rs1 AND-OR LUT -> alu_a LUT
    (the second forward level, merged with the is_auipc pc mux) -> 2 ALU LUTs
    (u_alu/n47) -> SIX result-mux LUTs (n1134_s16/s13/s9/s5/s3/s2 = the 11-arm alu_op
    case mux + the is_jump/is_muldiv mux) -> EX/MEM.alu_result. Paths 3/23/24 start at
    MEM/WB.wb_data (the second forward source).
 B) Redirect, 15.491 ns: pay_q.fwd_rs2_mwb -> 2 forward LUTs (rs2_1_s1/s0) ->
    br_diff 33-bit carry chain (1.9 ns incl. entry) -> 2 LUTs branch_cond/redirect
    (n1368_s4/s2) -> u_if/n69_s3 (CE = redirect|!stall, fanout 32) -> pc_hi_28_s4
    (fanout 30) -> pc_hi CE. This family covers pc_hi CE on 18 bits plus pc_hi D.
Both families begin with the same 2-LUT operand forward (5+ inputs: rs_val, exm,
alu_result_q, mwb, wb_data_q, plus the auipc/alu_src operand muxes). Everything else
in front of the endpoint is a select that ID already knows.

title: Decoupled front end: 2-entry bypassable fetch queue that prefetches during backend stalls to hide imem stalls
motivation:
With ~22% per-cycle imem backpressure, each fetch waits 0.28 cycles on
average. In the r3s0 champion, IF moves in lock-step with the backend:
whenever the backend stalls (dmem stall, load-use bubble, muldiv busy),
stall_if holds the PC, and the word the bus delivered that cycle is
thrown away and fetched again. Backend-stall cycles and imem-stall
cycles therefore add up instead of overlapping.
I measured this on r3s0 with the Verilator cosim (--istall --dstall):
2,937,037 retirements in 4,703,809 cycles, CPI 1.60. A cycle-level Python
model of the r3s0 pipeline, driven by the exact xorshift ready sequence
and the retired-instruction trace, gives 4,703,810 cycles, 1 cycle away
from the RTL. The same model with a bypassable fetch queue gives
1-entry 4,508,164 (-4.3%), 2-entry 4,478,156 (-5.0%) and 3-entry
4,476,030 (-5.1%) cycles. 2 entries capture almost all of the gain.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple IF from ID with a small bypassable fetch queue: 2 entries of
{pc[31:2], instr} in a shift-register FIFO whose head is entry 0.
- ID's instruction is `q_valid0 ? q_instr0 : io_imemData`, and valid is
  `q_valid0 | imem_ready`. This 2:1 mux has a flop select and replaces
  the existing `flush ? NOP : imem_data` mux in if_stage, so the imem ->
  regfile-address / decoder / load-use path keeps its LUT depth.
  Instead of forcing a NOP word, the flush-cleared ID/EX live bits
  (valid/reg_write/mem_rd/mem_wr/branch/jump/muldiv) are ANDed with the
  early IF/ID valid bit, which comes from a flop or IO, so side-effect
  bits stay clean for undelivered words.
- The fetch PC advances whenever imem is ready and the word has
  somewhere to go: `pc_adv = imem_ready && (!q_full || id_take)`, where
  id_take = ID/EX captures a real instruction (no dmem/md stall, no
  load-use). While the backend is stalled, delivered words are enqueued
  instead of discarded. While the queue is non-empty, an imem stall makes
  no bubble because ID drains the queue.
- Redirect has priority over everything, as today. It clears both queue
  valid bits and loads the PC. flush_id still kills the single wrong-path
  ID slot, so the taken-branch penalty stays 1 cycle. After a redirect
  the queue is empty and ID reads the bus directly again (no extra
  latency). Wrong-path words enqueued behind a taken branch are harmless
  because the redirect clears them before they can reach EX.
- hazard_unit: the queue's pc_adv replaces stall_if. flush_if goes away
  because valid gating moves to the live bits. stall_id / flush_id and the
  EX/MEM and MEM/WB controls are unchanged. load_use still compares the
  IF/ID rs1/rs2 fields (now from the head/bus mux) with ID/EX.rd.
- RVFI is unchanged: pc_rdata travels with the queue entry's pc.
Modeled gain: -5.0% cycles for 2 entries. The design adds no LUT level
on the EX path (the current critical path, ID/EX fwd select -> ALU ->
EX/MEM.alu_result). pc_adv is built from the same stall terms that drive
the PC CE today. The cost is about 70 FFs plus about 100 LUTs of queue
muxing, which lands on flop D inputs and not on critical cones. When the
queue is non-empty, ID even reads a flop instead of the BSRAM imem
output. Net expected fitness is about +5%, close to the 4.6% acceptance
bar, so the implementation must keep Fmax at >= 88.9 MHz. If `make timing`
shows the pc_adv/id_take cone in the top paths, compute
`imem_ready && !q_full` as the early term and OR id_take in as the only
late input.

title: Re-stack the lean IF predictor on r3s0: flop-fed predecode+BHT, mismatch-only EX redirect with a registered repair target, BHT trained from EX/MEM
motivation:
Champion r3s0 scores 190.01 iter/s: median Fmax 88.94 MHz (seeds 97.9 / 88.9 / 88.9)
and 4,680,666 timed cycles. That cycle count is identical to r2s0. The r3s0 gain came
entirely from Fmax, so every taken branch, JAL and JALR still costs one squashed IF
slot. The r1s2 trace study measured 0.122 redirect bubbles per instruction (18.1%
branches, 55.6% taken; 1.7% JAL; 0.47% JALR). That is about 7.6% of all cycles.

r3s2 already built the fix, a lean predictor, on the older r2s0 base. It cut the same
program from 4,680,666 to 4,382,792 cycles (-6.36%) and Fmax did not drop (61.9 ->
63.4 MHz). LESSONS.md says it lost only because r3s0 won that round with a different
base, and asks for a re-stack on r3s0 plus a timing check. At r3s0's 11.2 ns cycle
the new IF arm and the BHT update must stay short. The critical paths are now
fwd_rs1_exm -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result (15.5 ns, 11 cells) and, close behind, the
forwarded-operand branch compare -> redirect -> PC mux / ID/EX live bits. If the
predictor adds no LUT level to either path, the CPI gain goes straight to fitness:
190.01 x 4,680,666 / 4,382,792 = 202.9 (+6.8%), above the 4.6% acceptance bar.

Nothing in r3s0 changes the predictor's CPI profile. r3s0 and r2s0 retire the same
instruction stream in the same cycles, so r3s2's measured cycle saving should carry
over almost exactly.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Port r3s2's predictor onto the r3s0 RTL. Add three changes that keep every predictor
term off r3s0's EX critical paths:
- JAL is resolved entirely in IF.
- The BHT is trained from the EX/MEM register, not from EX.
- EX's redirect target comes from a flop.

1. IF (if_stage.sv): flop-fed prediction arm
   - Predecode io_imemData (on the FPGA bench this is an LFSR flop) for
     JAL (1101111) and BRANCH (1100011, funct3 != 2/3).
   - Pick the J- or B-immediate and compute pred_target[31:2] = pc_hi + imm[31:2]
     with one 30-bit adder. Both inputs are flops.
   - Direction comes from a 64 x 2-bit "agree with BTFN" counter table indexed by
     pc_hi[5:0] (pc[7:2]). Use async read and one sync write port, with no
     reset loop so it maps to LUT-RAM (syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram", the same
     idiom as reg_file.sv). Use an initial block that sets weakly-agree (2'b10).
     Counter MSB = 1 means "agree with static BTFN", and the BTFN direction is
     instr[31] (the imm sign).
   - pred_taken = !flush && !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_branch && (ctr[1] ~^ instr[31])))
     Written plainly: a branch is predicted taken iff (agree && backward) ||
     (!agree && forward), i.e. ctr[1] XNOR instr[31].
   - A misaligned target is never predicted, so the existing
     trap-without-redirect semantics stay exact.
   - Next-PC priority: redirect ? redirect_target : stall ? hold :
     pred_taken ? pred_target : pc_hi+1. The EX redirect stays the last mux level
     (the latest arm), as today. pred_taken needs no stall or redirect gating,
     because both higher-priority arms override it.
   - Export in if_id_t:
     * pred_taken
     * alt_pc[31:2] = pred_taken ? pc_hi+1 : pred_target (the repair PC if EX
       disagrees)
     * bht_ctr[1:0] (the counter value read, so training needs no second read port)
2. ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv)
   - Add alt_pc, bht_ctr and br_inv to the early-CE payload register, not the
     flush-cleared live bits. br_inv = funct3[0] ^ pred_taken.
   - They are only consumed under live_branch_q, which the existing flush clears, so
     the late flush fanout does not grow.
   - ID/EX captures an IF slot exactly when the PC advances using that same
     combinational prediction:
     * Any stall holds both the PC and ID/EX, or bubbles ID/EX.
     * An imem-stall slot is valid=0 with pred_taken=0.
     * A redirect flushes ID/EX.
     So the latched bits always describe the path that was actually fetched.
3. EX (ex_stage.sv): mismatch-only redirect with no added LUT levels
   - Today: branch_cond = op[2] ? (lt ^ op[0]) : (eq ^ op[0]).
     New: mismatch = op[2] ? (lt ^ br_inv_q) : (eq ^ br_inv_q). Same structure; one
     registered bit replaces another.
   - redirect = (is_branch && mismatch && !imm[1]) || (is_jalr && !agu[1]).
   - JAL never redirects from EX. IF always predicts an aligned JAL taken with the
     exact target, and a misaligned JAL traps without a redirect, as today. The
     is_jump && !is_jalr arm is dropped from the redirect OR (one fewer input on the
     redirect LUT).
   - redirect_target = is_jalr ? {agu[31:2],2'b00} : {alt_pc_q,2'b00}. This takes the
     pc+imm adder and its 30-bit mux off the redirect-target -> PC path; that
     adder now only feeds RVFI pc_next, which synthesis prunes.
   - Architectural branch_taken, pc_next, ctrl_with_trap, jump_misalign and the
     RVFI fields are computed exactly as today.
4. BHT training from EX/MEM, off the EX critical path
   - Add bht_ctr and the btfn bit (imm[31]) to ex_mem_t. EX/MEM already registers
     branch_taken, pc, ctrl.is_branch (live) and valid.
   - Write port: when EX/MEM.valid && EX/MEM.ctrl.is_branch, write
     counter[EX/MEM.pc[7:2]] <= sat(bht_ctr +/- 1), toward agree = (branch_taken ==
     btfn).
   - All write inputs are flops, so the compare -> taken path does not gain a
     LUT-RAM write-data or write-enable fanout.
   - The write is idempotent: the same registered data is written again if EX/MEM is
     held by a dmem stall, so no stall gating is needed.
   - Training arrives one cycle later than in r3s2. At 0.016 mispredicts per
     instruction that is noise.
5. Hazard unit: unchanged. flush_id still ORs redirect, which now fires only on a
   mispredict. The mispredict penalty stays at 1 killed slot. No RAS, no JALR
   prediction: JALR is under 0.3% of cycles.

Correctness argument:
- The prediction only changes which PC IF fetches next.
- EX recomputes the architectural outcome exactly as today, and redirects whenever
  the fetched successor differs from the architectural next PC:
  * predicted-taken, actually not taken -> alt_pc = pc+4
  * predicted not taken, actually taken -> alt_pc = pred_target = pc+imm
  * JALR -> agu
- riscv-formal (checks_si) and cosim cover this directly: pc_fwd/pc_bwd,
  unique and liveness all see the same retire stream.

Expected effect:
- Cycles: about -6.4%, as measured by r3s2 (4.68M -> ~4.38M).
- Area: about +110 LUT4 and +40 FF (one adder, a 64x2 LUT-RAM, the 30-bit alt_pc
  mux and flops).
- Fmax: should hold ~89 MHz. The IF arm is roughly LFSR flop -> imm select -> 30-bit
  carry chain -> 2 mux levels -> PC (~7-8 ns). The redirect enable and target get
  the same or lower depth.
- Fitness: about 190 x 1.068 = ~203 (+6-7%).

Fallback if `make timing` shows the pred_target adder or BHT read on the worst path:
predict only JAL plus backward branches (static BTFN, no table). The trace model keeps
about 70% of the gain that way.

title: Flat-slack sweep: trim one level from all six tied r4s0 limiter families (flop-fed DSP, NOP-free fetch word, 2-level redirect/flush, reset-free EX/MEM datapath)
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the r4s0 champion (place option 0: 107.3 MHz, 9.29 ns
data delay). The top 25 setup paths all lie within 0.13 ns (slack -4.32 .. -4.19) and form
SIX families. Fixing any one of them alone buys < 1%, and every one of them has a level
that is pure overhead:
 1) muldiv, -4.322, 7 cells: op_q[4] -> mul_a_32 LUT -> mul_b_32 LUT (op_q decode of the
    sign-extension bit, fanout 72 into the DSP) -> DSP 3.78 ns -> 3 LUTs
    (n1245_s16/s12/s11 = the op_q==MUL lo/hi select merged into result_q's
    state-dependent D mux) -> result_q.
 2) imem_ready, -4.312 (paths 2-4, 8, 9, 19, 25): imem_ready (fanout 72) -> u_if NOP mux
    on the instruction word (rs2_addr_w_1_s0, 0.95 ns net + 1 LUT) -> rd==rs2 carry-chain
    compare -> keep/take LUTs -> rs2_slot select (fanout 32) -> 2 slot LUTs ->
    pay_q.rs2_val.
 3) redirect -> flush, -4.292 (paths 5-7, 11-13, 17, 18, 23): pay_q.rs2_val -> fwd LUT ->
    br_diff 33-bit chain -> THREE redirect LUTs (u_if/n69_s6/s5/s3, fanout 31) ->
    flush_id LUT (n1417_s0) -> ID/EX live-bit RESET.
 4) redirect -> pc_hi D, -4.250 (paths 14, 15, 24): the same compare -> 3 redirect LUTs ->
    pc_hi mux.
 5) ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result, -4.263/-4.217 (paths 10, 20, 21): fwd LUT -> sum chain or
    barrel shifter -> 2 OR-tree LUTs -> 1 more LUT for EX/MEM's reset / stall-hold /
    bubble-clear before the flop.
 6) AGU -> dmem, -4.249 (paths 16, 22): Gowin retimes EX/MEM.mem_addr into the harness
    dmem BSRAM address register, so the path is fwd LUT -> agu chain -> n1470_s2 (hold
    mux) -> dmem_addr_c_b_b_b (reset/bubble clear) -> BSRAM ADB.
All six are CPI-neutral to fix, so this is the micro_opt slot. r4s0 showed that trimming
every tied family at once is what pays (+19.8%), and that plain relocation does not.

title: Decoupled front end on r4s0: 2-entry bypassable fetch queue (compares Shannon-split on the queue select) + capture-time muldiv sign decode
motivation:
The r4s0 champion scores 227.56 (107.3 MHz at option 0, 106.5 MHz median) over
4,680,666 cycles, CPI ~1.59. IF still runs in lock-step with the backend. On
every dmem-stall, load-use or muldiv-busy cycle, stall_if holds the PC, so the
word the bus delivered under the ~22% imem backpressure is thrown away and
fetched again. Since imem delivers at most 0.78 words/cycle, backend stalls and
fetch stalls add up instead of overlapping. r4s1 put a 2-entry bypassable fetch
queue on r3s0 and measured 4,455,961 cycles vs 4,680,666 (-4.8%, matching its
trace model's -5.0%). LESSONS says to re-stack it on r4s0.

`make timing TARGET=bench` on r4s0 (option 0), top setup paths (data delay):
  1) 9.287 ns muldiv: op_q -> mul_a_32 LUT -> mul_b_32 LUT (a/b_signed decode)
     -> DSP 3.78 ns -> 3-LUT hi/lo/result mux -> result_q.
  2) 9.277 ns stall_gen/imem_ready (fanout 72) -> if_stage NOP mux (rs2_addr)
     -> 5-bit rd==rs2 carry compare -> fwd decode -> rs2_slot selects
     (fanout 32) -> 2 LUTs -> ID/EX.rs2_val. Paths 2,3,4,8,9,19,25.
  3) 9.257 ns ID/EX.rs2_val -> EX fwd LUT (fanout 41) -> br_diff carry ->
     3 redirect LUTs (fanout 31) -> flush_id -> live-bit RESET / pc_hi D.
  4) 9.228 / 9.214 ns: EX ALU -> alu_result, AGU -> dmem BSRAM address.
In the FPGA bench io_imemData is an LFSR flop, so family 2's only late element
is the NOP mux and its fanout-72 select.
Honest expectation: removing families 1 and 2 leaves 3/4 within ~0.07 ns, so
Fmax gains ~0-3% (mostly a tighter spread across placement options). The main
gain is the queue's -4.8% cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Build on r4s0 unchanged (keep operand folding, one-hot AND-OR result, CE-free
pc_hi, live-bit split) and add the following.

A) Decoupled fetch: a 2-entry bypassable queue between imem and ID.
 - Entries {pc[31:2], instr, v} in a shift FIFO with the head at entry 0.
   ID's word is `q_v0 ? q_instr0 : io_imemData`, its pc is `q_v0 ? q_pc0 : pc`,
   and in.valid = q_v0 | imem_ready. This replaces if_stage's
   `flush ? NOP : imem_data` mux.
 - Kill undelivered words with the valid bit, not a NOP. AND in.valid (IO or
   flop, early) into the D input of every flush-cleared ID/EX live bit: valid,
   reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, branch, jump, muldiv, br_lt_go, br_eq_go,
   jal_go, jalr_go. Payload flops keep the plain !stall CE. load_use is left
   ungated: a spurious load_use from a garbage word only bubbles a slot that
   is already invalid.
 - id_take = !stall_id (= !(dmem_stall || load_use || md_stall)).
   pc_adv = imem_ready && (!q_full || id_take).
   pc_hi <= reset ? 0 : redirect ? target : pc_hi + {29'b0, pc_adv}, keeping
   r4s0's CE-free carry-in so redirect stays one mux level from pc_hi D.
 - Enqueue a delivered word that ID does not consume this cycle. Dequeue on
   id_take && q_v0, shifting entry 1 into entry 0. Redirect clears q_v0/q_v1
   (2 extra sync-reset endpoints on redirect). flush_id still kills the single
   wrong-path ID slot, so the taken-branch penalty stays 1 cycle, and after a
   redirect ID reads the bus directly again.
 - hazard_unit: drop flush_if and the imem_stall term of stall_if (the queue
   owns fetch advance). stall_id/flush_id and the EX/MEM and MEM/WB controls
   are unchanged. RVFI pc_rdata travels with the queue entry's pc.
 - IMPORTANT for Fmax: a plain q_v0-select mux would just relaunch family 2
   from q_v0 at the same depth (1 LUT plus a ~70-fanout select). Shannon-split
   the ID compares on the flop select instead. Compute the rd-vs-rs compares
   (id_ex_rd and ex_mem_rd against rs1/rs2, for rs?_exm, rs?_mwb and load_use)
   separately against q_instr0 and against io_imemData, both straight from
   flops, and fold q_v0 into the next LUT (e.g.
   rs2_exm = exm_wr & (q_v0 ? cmpQ : cmpB)). The head/bus mux then only feeds
   the LUT-RAM read address, the decoder and the imm path, which have slack.
   Replicate q_v0 if the tools do not.

   register a_signed_q, b_signed_q and hi_q, decoded from `op` (the ID/EX
   payload, early). The S_MUL product then uses

title: Re-stack the lean IF predictor on r4s0: prediction arm merged into the CE-free pc_hi update, redirect kept as the last MUX2 select, mismatch-only EX redirect
motivation:
The champion r4s0 scores 227.56 iter/s: 106.5 MHz median at 4,680,666 timed cycles.
That is the same cycle count as r2s0 and r3s0, so every taken branch and every JAL
still squashes one IF slot. The r1s2 trace study measured 0.122 redirect bubbles per
instruction, about 7.6% of all cycles. The same lean predictor has now been built
twice, and both times it cut cycles to 4,382,792 (-6.36%) without lowering Fmax:
  - r3s2 on r2s0: 132.16 -> 144.61
  - r4s2 on r3s0: 190.01 -> 223.06, about 98 MHz vs 88.9 MHz
In r4s2 Fmax actually rose, because the mismatch-only redirect took the JAL arm and
the pc+imm target mux out of the redirect cone.

Both times it lost only to an orthogonal Fmax fix in the same round. LESSONS.md asks
for a re-stack on r4s0 with two constraints:
  - merge the pred_target arm into r4s0's CE-free `pc_hi <= redirect ? tgt :
    pc_hi + !stall` update without adding a mux level between redirect and pc_hi D;
  - check that EX compare -> flush, one of r4s0's tied limiters, gains no level.
r4s0's other tied limiters (muldiv op_q -> result_q internal, and imem_ready ->
ID/EX.rs2_val) are not touched by a predictor. So the goal is to hold Fmax at ~106 MHz
and bank the cycle saving: 227.56 x 4,680,666 / 4,382,792 = 243.0 (+6.8%), above the
4.6% acceptance bar.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Port r4s2's predictor onto the r4s0 RTL. Keep every new term either on flop-fed
early paths or folded into bits EX already consumes.

1. IF (if_stage.sv): flop-fed prediction arm
   - Predecode the raw io_imemData word (not the flush-muxed NOP word). On the FPGA
     bench that word is an LFSR flop.
   - Detect JAL (1101111) and BRANCH (1100011 with funct3 != 2/3). Select the J- or
     B-immediate and compute pred_target[31:2] = pc_hi + imm[31:2] with one 30-bit
     carry chain. Both inputs are flops.
   - Direction comes from a 64 x 2-bit "agree with BTFN" table indexed by pc_hi[5:0]:
     * async read and one sync write port, no reset loop;
     * syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram", the same idiom as reg_file.sv;
     * initial block sets every entry to weakly-agree (2'b10);
     * predict taken iff ctr[1] XNOR instr[31] (agree and backward, or disagree and
       forward).
   - pred = imem_ready && !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_branch && (ctr[1] ~^ instr[31]))).
     A misaligned target is never predicted, so the existing trap-without-redirect
     semantics stay exact. imem_ready enters at the last AND.
   - Next-PC update keeps r4s0's shape and no CE:
       seq = pc_hi + {29'b0, !stall}        (existing carry-in)
       mid = (pred && !stall) ? pred_target : seq
       pc_hi <= redirect ? redirect_target[31:2] : mid
     Write it so that per bit, `mid` is one LUT4 of (take_pred, pred_target[i],
     seq[i]) and the redirect side is one LUT of redirect_target, with the late
     redirect as the select of a Gowin MUX2_LUT5 into the pc_hi D pin. Redirect then
     still sees one select level, as today. stall_if reaches D through one AND plus
     one LUT.
   - Export pred_taken in if_id_t: the ungated pred, already 0 on an imem-stall slot.
     ID/EX captures an IF slot exactly when the PC advances with that same
     prediction:
     * load_use, dmem_stall and md_stall hold the PC and hold or bubble ID/EX;
     * imem_stall makes the slot a valid=0 NOP;
     * redirect flushes ID/EX.
     So the latched bit always describes the path that was actually fetched.
   - Also export bht_ctr[1:0] (the value read) so training needs no second read port.
2. ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv)
   - In the early-CE payload, not the flush-cleared live bits:
     * br_inv <= instr[12] ^ pred_taken;
     * alt_pc[29:0] <= pred_taken ? (pc+4)[31:2] : (pc+imm)[31:2]. ID already
       computes both sums for pc4 and br_target.
     * bht_ctr, and a btfn bit (imm[31]).
   - Drop live_jal_go_q. Aligned JALs are always predicted taken in IF with the exact
     target, and misaligned JALs trap without a redirect, as today. The live-bit
     count and the flush fanout do not grow.
3. EX (ex_stage.sv): mismatch-only redirect with no added LUT level
   - redirect = (jalr_go && !agu[1]) || (br_lt_go && (br_lt ^ br_inv)) ||
     (br_eq_go && (br_eq ^ br_inv))
     This is r4s0's expression minus the jal_go input; br_inv now also carries the
     prediction.
   - redirect_target = jalr_go ? agu[31:2] : alt_pc_q. This is the same 2:1 shape as
     r4s0's jalr ? agu : br_target, with a registered operand.
   - Architectural branch_taken, pc_next, ctrl_with_trap, jump_misalign and all RVFI
     fields are computed exactly as today from the unmodified branch_op / funct3
     compare. Keep a separate registered funct3[0] for branch_cond so the RVFI and
     trap logic does not depend on the prediction.
4. BHT training from EX/MEM flops (core.sv wiring, ex_mem_t additions)
   - Write enable = EX/MEM.valid && EX/MEM.ctrl.is_branch.
   - Write address = EX/MEM.pc[7:2].
   - Write data = sat(bht_ctr +/- 1) toward agree = (branch_taken == btfn).
   - All inputs are flops, so the EX compare gains no fanout. Rewrites during a dmem
     hold write the same data (idempotent), so no stall gating is needed.
5. hazard_unit.sv: unchanged. flush_id still ORs redirect, which now fires only on a
   mispredict or a JALR. Mispredict penalty stays 1 slot. No RAS: JALR is about 0.3%
   of cycles, and a third 30-bit arm would add a level at pc_hi D.

Correctness:
- The prediction only changes which PC IF fetches next.
- EX recomputes the architectural outcome as today, and redirects whenever the
  fetched successor differs from the architectural next PC:
  * predicted taken, actually not taken: alt_pc = pc+4;
  * predicted not taken, actually taken: alt_pc = pc+imm;
  * JALR: agu.
- checks_si (pc_fwd/pc_bwd/unique/liveness) and cosim cover this directly.

Expected effect:
- Cycles: -6.36%, since r3s2 and r4s2 both measured exactly 4,382,792.
- Area: about +150 LUT4 and +40 FF.
- Fmax: should hold ~106 MHz. The new IF arm is LFSR flop -> opcode/imm select
  (1-2 LUT) -> 30-bit carry -> LUT4 -> MUX2 -> pc_hi. The BHT path is pc_hi ->
  RAM16 read -> 4:1 MUX2 -> XNOR/AND -> take_pred fanout-30. Both are well under
  9.4 ns, and the redirect and flush depths are unchanged.

Implementer: run `make timing` before finishing. If a pc_hi D or take_pred path shows
up among the top paths above r4s0's ~9.4 ns limiters, first drop the BHT and keep
static BTFN + JAL (about 70% of the gain). Only then consider other changes.
